q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT b1.name, b2.name FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT beer FROM serves WHERE b1.name = serves.bar AND NOT serves.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM serves WHERE b2.name = serves.bar))

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they check for different conditions regarding the beers served by bars. Q1 checks for beers that are served by a bar b1 but not by any other bar b2, and also for beers that are served by a bar b2 but not by b1. Q2, on the other hand, checks for beers that are served by a bar b1 but not by any other bar b2, without the reverse condition.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two bars, b1 and b2, where b1 serves beer x but not beer y, and b2 serves beer y but not beer x. This should trigger a difference in the results of Q1 and Q2.
